title: Supplier request
requirement: Any employee with the request permission shall ask for a new supplier: its name, country, a contact's email when known, the reason, the category, the unit that will buy, the expected spend over the next twelve months, and the urgency. While the name or a tax identifier is typed, existing suppliers and likely duplicates are shown with their status and the units they are enabled in (SUP-003); a supplier already enabled for the unit is offered instead of a request. A request also reopens a deactivated supplier (SUP-025).
rationale: Requesters know they need a supplier long before a buyer does. A request with its reason, category and spend lets procurement decide whether a new supplier is needed at all, and starts onboarding with the facts it needs; the leading suites start here.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requester typing a name similar to an existing supplier, When the matches appear, Then each shows its status and the units it is enabled in.|Given a match already enabled for the requester's unit, When the requester chooses it, Then no request is made and the requester is told the supplier can be used.|Given a request without a reason or a category, When submitted, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)|Given a person without the request permission, When they submit a request, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G1 of the supplier management pack). Map steps SM-01 and SM-02.

title: Supplier request approval
requirement: A supplier request shall run the supplier request approval configuration (BF-141), with its expected spend, category, unit, country and urgency as registered fields. A buyer or supplier manager reviews it for duplicates and existing suppliers (SM-02). An approved request becomes the invitation of a new supplier (SUP-001), or, when the reviewer finds the supplier already exists, its enablement for the unit (BF-108, SUP-006). A refused request is closed with its reasons and the requester is told (E6). An approved request whose invitation expires or whose registration is abandoned is reminded, resent, or closed with a reason (E5). Until the supplier side exists, a buyer creates the supplier from an approved request, within what its risk tier allows (SUP-005).
rationale: Only a supplier someone needs, and that procurement agreed to, should start onboarding; the decision belongs before the supplier is asked to do any work.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request above the spend threshold of a configuration, When submitted, Then it is in approval with that configuration's approvers.|Given a reviewer who finds that the supplier exists, When they mark the request so, Then the supplier's enablement for the unit starts and the requester is told.|Given a request refused, When decided, Then it is closed with the reasons and the requester is told.|Given a refusal without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an approved request whose invitation expired unanswered, When the buyer closes it, Then a reason is required, and the requester is told.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G1). Map steps SM-02 and SM-03, exceptions E5 and E6. The invitation itself is SUP-001's, which since 2026-10-21 starts from an approved request (SUP-001 AC5). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a request is required before every invitation unless the tenant turns the setting off; a buyer may raise a request, which the configuration may approve at once.

title: Supplier invitation
requirement: A buyer with the invite permission shall invite a supplier (company name, country, primary contact email or network identifier, optional category and documents to sign), creating a supplier in Invited status in the tenant and a relationship invitation in the Supplier Network, which matches an existing network organisation by tax identifier or email domain or sends a time-limited registration link (72 hours, resendable); duplicates in the tenant shall be flagged before sending. Where the tenant requires a supplier request, which it does by default, an invitation starts only from an approved request (SUP-142) and carries the request's data.
rationale: Start of onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new company and contact, When invited, Then the supplier exists as Invited and the email is sent.|Given a company that matches an existing supplier by tax identifier or name similarity, When invited, Then a duplicate warning lists the matches and requires confirmation. (error case)|Given an expired link, When resent, Then a new link is sent and the old one stops working.|Given the supplier already exists in the network, When invited, Then the existing organisation receives a connection request instead of a registration link. (edge)|Given a tenant that requires a supplier request, When a buyer invites a supplier without an approved request, Then it is refused naming the missing request. (error case)|Given an approved request, When the buyer invites from it, Then the invitation is pre-filled with the request's name, country, contact and category, and links back to the request.
notes: Was FF-020. Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G1): an invitation starts from an approved supplier request where the tenant requires one (AC5, AC6).

title: Supplier self-registration
requirement: A new supplier shall register once in the Supplier Network (credentials, MFA, terms, network profile: legal name, country, tax identifiers, one contact); an existing supplier shall accept the connection; then the customer-specific wizard with sections enabled per tenant (addresses, contacts, sites, bank accounts, tax and compliance, documents, questionnaires) pre-fills from the network profile, saves progress and submits when mandatory sections are complete.
rationale: Supplier self-service.
acceptance_criteria: Given mandatory sections complete, When submitted, Then the supplier moves to Registered and the buyer is notified.|Given a mandatory document missing, When submitted, Then the section and document are named and submission is refused. (error case)|Given progress saved, When the contact returns, Then the wizard resumes where they left.
notes: Was FF-021. Since 2026-10-21 it depends on SUP-005, whose enabled sections it shows, and SUP-005 no longer on it, so the onboarding configuration can come before the supplier side (the technical PRD's section 7.2).

title: Duplicate supplier detection
requirement: On create and on registration the system shall check exact matches (tax identifiers, registration numbers, email, phone, bank account) and fuzzy matches (name and address similarity above a configurable threshold) and show candidates; a buyer may mark a candidate as "not a duplicate" with a reason.
rationale: Duplicate suppliers break spend analysis and payments.
acceptance_criteria: Given a name similar above the threshold, When saved, Then candidates are shown and confirmation required.|Given an exact tax identifier match, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a candidate marked not duplicate, When saved again, Then it is not shown again for that pair.
notes: Was FF-023.

title: Supplier approval and publishing
requirement: New suppliers shall run the supplier-new approval configuration; approved suppliers shall be published only when publishing criteria are met (mandatory documents valid, required sections complete, at least one active contact, bank account verified when required, the information requests its risk tier requires approved, its identifiers verified and its sanctions screening clear); unpublishing shall remove the supplier from selection on new documents. With regulated qualification, a quality-relevant material is bought only through an approved combination of the supplier, its site and the material (SUP-183).
rationale: Only vetted suppliers receive orders.
acceptance_criteria: Given criteria met, When published, Then the supplier can be selected on requests and orders.|Given an expired mandatory document, When publishing, Then it is refused naming the document. (error case)|Given unpublished, When a new request line is edited, Then the supplier is not offered and existing documents keep it.|Given an information request its risk tier requires and that is not yet approved, When publishing, Then it is refused naming the request. (error case)|Given a supplier on hold after a possible sanctions match, When publishing, Then it is refused naming the screening case. (error case)
notes: Was FF-024. Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gaps G4, G6 and G12): the publishing criteria take the information requests the risk tier requires, the identifier verification and the sanctions screening (AC4, AC5); a required information request replaces the required questionnaire of SUP-042, retired.

title: Supplier onboarding configuration
requirement: Settings for enabled registration sections and for what a new supplier must meet, chosen by its risk tier (SUP-007), its categories and its country: the sections, documents and information requests (SUP-222) it must complete, the checks it must pass (SUP-161 to SUP-165) and the approvals it needs; bank verification rules and duplicate thresholds. A supplier created by a buyer without a registration (variant V1) is allowed only in the lowest risk tier. The channels a new supplier starts with are the supplier portal's, its terms the supplier master's.
rationale: Different onboarding per tenant, and per supplier: a low-risk supplier of office supplies should not wait for what a supplier of active ingredients must show, and a high-risk one must not get through on a low-risk path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a section disabled, When a supplier registers, Then it is not shown.|Given the call-back required for a risk tier, When a bank account of a supplier of that tier is approved without the call-back recorded, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a threshold changed, When duplicate detection runs, Then the new threshold applies.|Given a document set as required for new suppliers, When a supplier is invited, Then the document is listed among what it must complete.|Given requirements set for risk tier high, category chemicals and country India, When a supplier of that tier, category and country is invited, Then exactly those sections, documents, information requests, checks and approvals are listed among what it must complete.|Given a supplier of a risk tier above the lowest, When a buyer creates it without a registration, Then it is refused naming the tier. (error case)
notes: Was FF-171, FF-035 and BF-106: FF-171 whole, with the sections and documents BF-106 set for a new supplier merged in at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043). Its portal channels moved to the supplier portal (SPX-007); the supplier defaults it named are BF-106's and PUR-024's. Rewritten 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G12): what a new supplier must meet is chosen by risk tier, category and country, and the buyer-created supplier is allowed only in the lowest tier (AC5, AC6); AC2 now names the call-back of SUP-163, which replaced SUP-023's checklist. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: when the requirements of several categories or countries apply, the supplier must meet all of them. It comes with Supplier management in the tenant (PR1), and its registration sections reach the supplier with the registration wizard (SUP-002, PR8).

title: Organisation approval of an enablement
requirement: Enabling a supplier in an organisation (BF-108) shall run an optional organisation approval.
rationale: One registration for the supplier, separate control for each unit.
acceptance_criteria: Given organisation approval required in organisation A, When a supplier is enabled in A, Then the enablement takes effect when the approval completes.|Given an enablement in organisation A still in approval, When a buyer of A creates an order for the supplier, Then it is refused naming the pending approval. (error case)
notes: Was FF-182, its optional organisation approval; the enablement is BF-108. AC1 and AC2 are written for the split from the requirement's own clauses.

title: Supplier risk tier
requirement: Each supplier shall have a risk tier, low, medium, high or critical, computed by the tenant's tier rules from its categories, its country, its spend over the last twelve months and its screening and verification results, the highest tier any rule gives winning; a permitted user may change it by hand with a reason. The tier decides what onboarding requires (SUP-005), the intervals of re-verification and requalification (SUP-161, SUP-181), whether a bank change needs the call-back (SUP-163), and how changes are routed (SUP-204). Every change of tier is recorded with its reason, and when the tier rises, what the new tier requires and the supplier lacks is raised and the buyer owner is told. The tier is computed at registration, after every screening or verification result, and each night for spend; it answers the purchasing master's supplier facts with the spend (PUR-026).
rationale: The same checks for every supplier are too slow for the low-risk ones and too light for the risky ones; the leading suites and ISO 9001 (clause 8.4) set the extent of control by risk.
acceptance_criteria: Given a rule that category chemicals is high and a supplier in chemicals, When its tier is computed, Then it is high, with the rule named.|Given two rules that give medium and high, When the tier is computed, Then it is high.|Given a possible sanctions match or a failed verification recorded, When the result arrives, Then the tier is computed again at once.|Given a tier changed by hand without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a supplier whose tier rises from medium to high, When it changes, Then the information requests and checks high requires and the supplier lacks are raised, and the buyer owner is told.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G12 of the supplier management pack). Its spend comes from the order issued events, as the indicators' counts do (SUP-062, ADR-0042). The risk tier is the eProcurement Suite's, not the Foundation's (ADR-0043, decision 8). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: four tiers, low, medium, high and critical, with the highest rule winning, and the times it is computed.

title: Identifier re-verification
requirement: A supplier's identifiers shall be verified through the identity and tax status connectors (TF-206) at registration and again on a schedule set by risk tier and country: for India, the GSTIN's registration status, the PAN's status and that the PAN is the one inside the GSTIN, and the Udyam classification (BF-204); elsewhere, the checks the country's connector offers. A result that differs from the record creates a change request from the source re-verification (SUP-201) for the fields it touches, and the tenant's rules decide whether the supplier goes on hold until a person decides. Each result is kept with its date, the provider's reference and its outcome.
rationale: A tax registration valid at onboarding may be cancelled a year later; an Indian buyer that keeps paying GST to a supplier whose GSTIN is cancelled loses the input tax credit, and a changed MSME classification changes how fast the supplier must be paid.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier of tier high last verified three months ago, When the schedule runs, Then its identifiers are verified again and the result is kept with its date.|Given a GSTIN found cancelled, When the result arrives, Then the supplier is put on hold with the result as the reason, a change request records the new status, and the buyer owner is told.|Given a Udyam enterprise type found changed from micro to small, When the result arrives, Then a change request from the source re-verification proposes the new type, as a critical field (SUP-202).|Given no connector for the supplier's country, When the schedule runs, Then the check is recorded as not available, and the buyer owner is told once. (error case)|Given a provider that does not answer, When the check runs, Then it is retried, and after the last retry it is recorded as failed and listed for review, the supplier's status unchanged. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G4). Map steps SM-05 and V6, source C4 of the change management map. Its connectors come with the kernel's S7 (TF-206); until then the verification at registration is the buyer's, recorded by hand. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: identifiers are verified again every year for tiers low and medium and every quarter for high and critical, and a cancelled or suspended tax registration puts the supplier on hold.

title: Automated bank account verification
requirement: A bank account added or changed shall be verified automatically where the country allows it: for India, a penny-drop or an NPCI name match; elsewhere, the IBAN's check digits and the BIC (ISO 13616, ISO 9362) and the holder's name through the bank account connector (TF-206). The result (whether the account exists, and whether the holder's name matched, matched in part, or did not) is kept with its date and the provider's reference. A name that does not match fails the verification; a partial match goes to a reviewer, who sees both names. The verification is a hook of the bank change (SUP-205): the account applies only after it passes.
rationale: A manual check alone misses what a bank can confirm in seconds: that the account exists and belongs to the supplier. Bank account change fraud is the main payables risk, and business email compromise cost about 3 billion US dollars of reported losses in 2025.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Indian account whose penny-drop returns the supplier's legal name, When verified, Then the verification passes and the result is kept with the provider's reference.|Given an IBAN with a wrong check digit, When entered, Then it is refused before any provider is asked. (error case)|Given a holder's name that does not match, When verified, Then the verification fails, the account does not apply, and the change request records why. (error case)|Given a partial name match, When verified, Then the change request waits for a reviewer's decision, with both names shown.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G5); with SUP-163, SUP-164 and SUP-205 it replaces SUP-023, retired. Map steps SM-06 and CM-05. Its connectors come with the kernel's S7 (TF-206); until then every bank change needs the call-back (SUP-163).

title: Bank account call-back
requirement: A bank account shall be verified out of band by a call-back where no automated check is available for its country, and, beside the automated check, for the risk tiers the tenant names: the approver calls the supplier at a number known before the change, never one given in it, records who confirmed, when and how, and attaches the evidence. A bank change that needs the call-back cannot be approved until it is recorded, and the approver is a second person, never the one who entered the change.
rationale: Bank account change fraud is the main payables risk; a call to a number the fraudster supplied proves nothing, and an automated check cannot tell a supplier from a fraudster who controls the supplier's mailbox. Decision F-05 asked for a second approver and an out-of-band check.
acceptance_criteria: Given a bank change for a supplier of a tier that needs the call-back, When the approver opens it, Then the call-back checklist is shown with the numbers known before the change, and approval waits for it.|Given a call-back recorded to a number that came with the change, When saved, Then it is refused naming the number. (error case)|Given a bank change that needs the call-back, When it is approved without one recorded, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a country with no automated check, When a low-tier supplier's bank account changes, Then the call-back is required.|Given the person who entered a bank change, When they approve it, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New in this area 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G5): the checklist of SUP-023, retired, kept as the call-back. Map steps SM-06 and CM-05. Decision F-05 asked for the checklist on every bank change; gap G5 keeps it for the critical tiers beside an automated check. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: the call-back is required wherever no automated check is available, and beside one for the tier critical by default, which the tenant may widen.

title: Cooling period and the payment check
requirement: After a bank account is added or changed, a cooling period (3 business days by default, by the tenant's business calendar, TF-099) shall pass before the first payment to it. Supplier management answers, through its Contracts, whether an account may be paid on a date, and to whom: the account must be verified, valid on that date and out of its cooling period; for an account changed within the re-check window (30 days by default), the answer first runs the check again (the automated check, or the call-back where none is available); and the answer names the people who requested and approved the account's change, whom the releasing product refuses as the releaser within the cooling period (TF-036).
rationale: A fraudulent bank change is often followed at once by a payment run. A few days' wait, and a fresh check of a recently changed account, give the supplier's real contacts, told of the change through the channels they had before it (SUP-205), the time to object.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account changed on a Monday and a cooling period of 3 business days, When asked whether it may be paid on Wednesday, Then the answer is no, naming the first day it may be.|Given an account changed 10 days ago, When asked on the payment date, Then the account is checked again first, and the answer is yes only when the check passes.|Given an account not verified, When asked, Then the answer is no, naming the verification it waits for. (error case)|Given a re-check that fails, When it returns, Then the answer is no, the account goes back to unverified, and the buyer owner and finance are told. (error case)|Given an account verified and changed 40 days ago, When asked, Then the answer is yes without a new check.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G5). Map step CM-07. Invoicing asks it at payment release (INV-046), since a later product calls an earlier one (ADR-0042). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: the pack asks for a re-check at payment release for accounts changed within the period, which would never fire if the cooling period blocked every payment in it; the reading is a cooling period of 3 business days in which nothing is paid, and a re-check window of 30 days in which every release checks again.

title: Sanctions and watch-list screening
requirement: Suppliers shall be screened through the sanctions connector (TF-206), with their legal name, trade names and country, at registration (SM-05), on a schedule, when the provider reports a change of a list, and when a change to the legal name, a trade name or the country applies (SUP-201). A possible match puts the supplier on hold (SUP-021) with the match as the reason and opens a compliance case; compliance decides, with the evidence kept (the list entry, the provider's answer, the decision, who decided and when): a true match keeps the supplier on hold or offboards it (SUP-025); a false positive is cleared with a reason, and is not raised again for the same list entry unless the entry changes.
rationale: Paying a sanctioned party breaks the law wherever the tenant operates; screening only at onboarding misses the parties listed later.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new registration, When the checks run at SM-05, Then the supplier is screened before it can be approved.|Given a possible match, When the result arrives, Then the supplier is on hold, compliance has a case with the list entry, and nothing can be ordered from it.|Given a match cleared as a false positive, When the next screening returns the same list entry unchanged, Then no new case is opened and the clearance is cited.|Given the same list entry changed by its list, When screened, Then a new case is opened.|Given a person outside compliance, When they decide a case, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given screening unavailable at registration, When the checks run, Then approval waits and the buyer owner is told; a supplier is not approved unscreened. (error case)|Given an approved supplier whose legal name changes, When the change applies, Then the supplier is screened again with the new name, and the same for a trade name or the country.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G6). Map steps SM-05 and V6, exception E3. Its connector comes with the kernel's S7 (TF-206). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: screening runs monthly by default, on every list change the provider reports, and when a change to the legal name, a trade name or the country applies (AC7, added at the review); the names screened are the legal and trade names with the country.

title: Qualification by scope
requirement: A supplier's qualification shall be held per scope: a category, a region, a unit, or, with regulated qualification, a manufacturing site and material (SUP-183). Each has a status: pending, qualified, conditionally qualified (with its conditions and an end date), disqualified (with a reason), or requalification due. The tenant names which scopes require qualification, and for each the evidence (information requests, documents, an audit when required) and its approvers. Requalification is scheduled by risk tier and runs as an information request (SUP-223); a conditional qualification past its end date becomes requalification due. Supplier management answers the purchasing master's question whether a supplier is qualified for a scope (PUR-022), and reports through the master's Contracts when a qualification ends.
rationale: One approval for every purpose either over-checks a supplier of paper or under-checks a supplier of reagents. Qualification per category, region or unit, with preferred status only where qualified, is what the leading suites offer and what ISO 9001 (clause 8.4) asks.
acceptance_criteria: Given category laboratory chemicals requires qualification, When a supplier's evidence for it is approved, Then its status for that category is qualified, with the date and the approvers.|Given a conditional qualification ending on 31 March, When the date passes, Then its status becomes requalification due and the buyer owner is told.|Given a qualified scope whose requalification falls due, When the date comes, Then an information request for the requalification is sent and the status shows requalification due.|Given a supplier disqualified for a category, When a buyer sets it preferred for that category, Then it is refused naming the qualification (PUR-022). (error case)|Given a disqualification without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a scope that requires no qualification, When the purchasing master asks, Then the answer is not required.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G2); SUP-042's qualification questionnaires, retired, are its evidence through supplier information collection. Map steps SM-07 and V6. It implements the purchasing master's extension point for qualification (PUR-022, the purchasing PRD's section 8.5). One qualification entity with a scope kind (the pack's section 8.5, decision 4). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: no scope requires qualification until the tenant names it, and requalification falls due every 3 years for tier low, 2 for medium and 1 for high and critical.

title: Quality-relevant items and categories
requirement: With the licensed feature `supplier_management.gxp_qualification` (TF-046), the quality unit shall mark items and categories as quality-relevant: an item is quality-relevant when it is marked or its category is. A quality-relevant material is bought only from an approved combination of supplier, manufacturing site and material (SUP-183). Marking and unmarking are audited with who and why. Without the feature nothing is marked, and no rule of regulated qualification applies.
rationale: In a regulated plant only some materials affect product quality (EU GMP chapter 5.26: starting materials only from approved suppliers); marking them tells every product which purchases the quality unit controls.
acceptance_criteria: Given the feature on, When the quality unit marks an item quality-relevant, Then the item shows it and the audit records who marked it and why.|Given a category marked quality-relevant, When an item of that category is created, Then it is quality-relevant.|Given the feature off, When the marking is asked for on the screen or through the API, Then it is refused with the not-entitled code. (error case)|Given a person outside the quality unit, When they mark or unmark an item, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G3, variant V4). The marking is held by Supplier management for the items and categories of the Business masters, since it belongs to the licensed feature, not to every tenant's items.

title: Regulated qualification: the approved supplier list
requirement: With the feature, the approved supplier list shall hold, for each supplier, manufacturing site (BF-104, purpose manufacturing) and quality-relevant material, a qualification of the scope site and material (SUP-181): its status, its evidence (information responses, documents, audits, SUP-184), the risk assessment that sets its requalification interval, and the quality agreement in force, which Contracts reports through its events (CON-007). The quality unit approves a combination with an electronic signature (TF-063, meaning approved, re-authentication required) and may approve it conditionally, with its conditions shown to buyers. Supplier management answers, through its Contracts, whether a supplier, site and material may be ordered: an approved combination may, and a conditionally approved one may too, with its conditions, unless the tenant's setting is approved only.
rationale: A regulated buyer must show an inspector that every starting material came from a supplier and site the quality unit approved for it, under a written agreement (EU GMP chapters 5 and 7, Annex 16; ICH Q7, Q9 and Q10). Procurement suites leave this to quality systems; holding it where orders are placed closes the gap between the two.
acceptance_criteria: Given evidence complete for a supplier, its site in Pune and material 4711, When the quality unit approves with re-authentication, Then the combination is approved, and the signature shows the signer's name, the time and the meaning.|Given an approval without re-authentication, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a tenant that requires a quality agreement and a combination without one in force, When approval is attempted, Then it is refused naming the missing agreement. (error case)|Given a site that does not serve the manufacturing purpose, When it is chosen for a combination, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given the combination of Pune and material 4711 approved, When Orders asks whether that supplier may supply material 4711 from Pune, Then the answer is yes; from its site in Mumbai, no, naming the missing approval.|Given a conditionally approved combination and a tenant whose setting is approved only, When Orders asks whether it may be ordered, Then the answer is no, naming the conditional approval; with the default setting the answer is yes, with its conditions. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G3, variant V4). Map steps SM-07 and SM-09. The approved supplier list is the one qualification entity with the scope site and material (the pack's section 8.5, decision 4). Orders checks it at submission (ORD-010). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a quality agreement in force is required before approval by default, which the tenant may turn off; a conditional approval allows ordering by default, a tenant setting that a strict tenant switches to approved only (AC6).

title: Supplier audits and findings
requirement: With the feature, audits of a supplier and its sites shall be recorded: type (on site, remote, or on paper), date, auditors, scope and outcome; each finding with its classification (critical, major or minor), the corrective and preventive action agreed, its owner, its due date, and its closure with evidence. A combination with an open critical finding cannot be approved, and an approved one that receives a critical finding becomes conditionally qualified until the quality unit decides.
rationale: An audit is the strongest evidence of qualification, and its findings are the follow-up an inspector asks to see closed.
acceptance_criteria: Given an audit with two findings, When recorded, Then each finding has its classification, action, owner and due date.|Given an open critical finding, When approval of its combination is attempted, Then it is refused naming the finding. (error case)|Given an action past its due date, When the daily job runs, Then its owner and the quality unit are told.|Given a finding closed without evidence, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G3). Map steps SM-07 and V6. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a new critical finding turns an approved combination conditional at once, rather than leaving the decision to the quality unit alone.

title: Supplier status control
requirement: Permitted users shall put a supplier on hold, release and deactivate it, with a mandatory reason; hold and deactivation shall warn when open orders, receipts in approval or submitted invoices exist and shall require a second confirmation; deactivation runs the offboarding checklist (SUP-025), and a deactivated supplier comes back only through a supplier request that reopens it (SUP-141); on hold or inactive suppliers shall not be selectable and their portal users shall see a status notice.
rationale: Carried; adds guards and reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Given open orders, When deactivation is requested, Then the list of open documents is shown and confirmation is required.|Given a supplier on hold, When a buyer creates an order for it, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a deactivated supplier needed again, When a buyer tries to reactivate it by changing its status, Then it is refused, naming the supplier request that reopens it. (error case)|Given a supplier released from hold, When released, Then its previous published status is restored.
notes: Was FF-025. Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G8): deactivation runs the offboarding checklist, and reactivation became re-onboarding through a request (AC3); release from hold restores the published status, as reactivation did (AC4).

title: Supplier change approval
requirement: Changes to approved suppliers (by supplier or buyer) in controlled fields (legal name, tax identifiers, bank, addresses, contacts) shall run the supplier-change approval configuration; uncontrolled fields apply immediately; pending changes shall be visible side by side with current values.
rationale: Control over master changes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a controlled field changed, When saved, Then the record keeps current values until approval and shows the pending change.|Given rejection, When done, Then the change is discarded and the proposer notified.|Given an uncontrolled field changed, When saved, Then it applies at once with history. (edge)|Given a change to a controlled field by a user without permission, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-033. Retired 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps): supplier information change management (the pack's section 8.2) rewrote it into an area of its own, with field classes, decisions per field, routing, segregation, effective dates, concurrency, the impact preview, notifications, signatures and measures, on the kernel's governed changes (TF-247). Replaced by SUP-201 to SUP-204 and SUP-206 to SUP-211.

title: Supplier bank account verification
requirement: Any addition or change of a supplier's bank account shall run an approval with a mandatory out-of-band verification checklist (call-back to a known number, document check) recorded by the approver; changes shall notify the supplier's primary contact and the buyer owner.
rationale: Bank account change fraud is the main payables risk.
acceptance_criteria: Given a bank change by a supplier user, When submitted, Then the approver sees the checklist and cannot approve until it is completed.|Given a change approved without the checklist, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a change, When saved, Then the primary contact and the buyer owner are notified.
notes: Was FF-029, the verification; the account data is BF-105. Decision F-05 confirmed. Retired 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps): a bank change became a critical change of supplier information change management, verified automatically where the country allows it and by call-back as required, with a cooling period before the first payment (gap G5, the pack's section 8.2). Replaced by SUP-162 to SUP-164 and SUP-205.

title: Supplier merge
requirement: A permitted user shall merge a duplicate supplier into a surviving supplier, moving documents, contacts and portal users, with a preview and an audit of the merge; the merged supplier becomes inactive with a pointer to the survivor.
rationale: Clean master data.
acceptance_criteria: Given a merge preview, When confirmed, Then all documents reference the survivor and the duplicate is inactive.|Given a merge of suppliers with different tax identifiers, When attempted, Then a warning requires confirmation. (edge)|Given a merge, When audited, Then the full list of moved records is recorded.|Given a merge requested by a user without the merge permission, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-037.

title: Offboarding
requirement: Before a supplier is deactivated, an offboarding checklist shall be completed: its open orders, receipts in approval and submitted invoices listed, each closed, cancelled or moved, or the deactivation confirmed with them open by a permitted user with a reason; its portal users' access to this tenant removed and its one-time links revoked (TF-246); its records given the retention class relationship ended, from which their retention period runs (TF-066); and the reason recorded. A deactivated supplier is re-onboarded only through a supplier request (SUP-141) that reopens the same record, with its history kept, and its checks and approvals run again by its risk tier.
rationale: Deactivation alone leaves open documents, portal access and data behind. A clean end, and a clean way back that keeps the history, protects the tenant and the supplier both.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier with two open orders, When deactivation starts, Then the checklist lists both, and deactivation waits until each is closed, cancelled or moved, or a permitted user confirms with a reason.|Given the checklist complete, When the supplier is deactivated, Then its portal users lose access to this tenant, its open links are revoked, and its records carry the retention class with the day's date.|Given a deactivation without a reason, When confirmed, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a deactivated supplier, When a requester asks for it again and the request is approved, Then the same record reopens with its history, and it is published only after its checks and approvals run again.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G8). Map step V7, the open documents counted from the events of Orders, Receiving and Invoicing (section 12.3). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a permitted user may deactivate with open documents and a reason, and the retention class is named relationship ended.

title: Change requests for every change
requirement: A change to an approved supplier (its record, BF-101 to BF-108; its purchasing profile, PUR-021 to PUR-024; this product's documents) shall never be written straight to the record. It becomes a change request on the kernel's governed changes (TF-247): the supplier, its source, who asked, a reason, evidence, an effective date, and each field's old and new values. The sources are: a buyer's edit; the supplier's edit in the portal; an approved information response (SUP-227); a re-verification result (SUP-161); an import or ERP sync (BF-206); and a change to the supplier's network profile, offered to each connected customer (SUP-101). A supplier not yet approved changes its data within onboarding.
rationale: One pipeline for every source, with its classes, approvals and verification, is the only way to be sure that no change, from a person, an import or a form, bypasses them.
acceptance_criteria: Given a buyer editing an approved supplier's address, When saved, Then a change request with the old and new address exists, and the record still holds the old one.|Given an ERP sync that brings a new legal name, When it runs, Then a change request from the source ERP sync is made, not a direct update.|Given a call to the API that writes a supplier field directly, When made, Then it is refused, naming the change request as the way. (error case)|Given a buyer's change request without a reason, When submitted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2). Map step CM-01 and its sources C1 to C6. With SUP-202 to SUP-204 and SUP-206 to SUP-211 it replaces SUP-022, retired.

title: Field classes of the supplier record
requirement: Every field and section of the supplier record (BF-101 to BF-108, PUR-021 to PUR-024) shall have a class, set per tenant from these defaults. Uncontrolled: the descriptive fields (website, description, logo, the trade name's display form), applied at once, recorded, and the buyer owner told. Controlled: addresses other than the remit-to address, contacts other than those that receive orders or payment advice, sites, categories, documents, diversity and classification attributes, and the terms per unit; approved by the configured approvers before they apply. Critical: bank accounts, the legal name, tax identifiers, the remit-to address, the contacts that receive orders or payment advice, and the Udyam classification; approved, then verified, then applied, and a bank change starts the cooling period. A tenant may raise a field's class; a critical field stays critical.
rationale: Each class matches its risk: a new logo needs no approver, a new bank account needs two people and a bank's confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Given the defaults, When a supplier's website changes, Then it applies at once, is in the history, and the buyer owner is told.|Given the defaults, When the contact who receives payment advice changes, Then the change is approved, then verified, then applied.|Given a tenant that raises sites to critical, When a site changes, Then it is approved, verified and applied as a critical change.|Given a tenant that lowers bank accounts to controlled, When the classes are saved, Then it is refused naming the field and its floor. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2). Map step CM-02. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: the critical fields' floor is critical, so no tenant can let a bank account change without verification, while a controlled field may be set uncontrolled.

title: Decisions per field
requirement: A reviewer shall approve or reject each field change, with a reason for each rejection, or return a question to the requester (the supplier, when the supplier asked). A change request may end partly applied; the requester sees which changes applied, which were rejected and why, and which wait.
rationale: A supplier that sends a new address and a wrong phone number should not lose the address because of the phone; and it must know what the customer did with each.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request with an address and a phone change, When the address is approved and the phone rejected with a reason, Then the address applies, the phone does not, and the supplier sees both outcomes with the reason.|Given a rejection without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a question returned to the supplier, When the supplier answers in the portal, Then the field goes back to the reviewer with the answer.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 1). Map step CM-04, and the question back to source C2.

title: Routing and segregation
requirement: Change requests shall be routed through the approval configurations (BF-141) of the document type supplier change, with the field class, the supplier's risk tier (SUP-007) and the unit as registered fields; a change to one unit's terms goes to that unit's approvers. Nobody approves a change they requested, and nobody who requested or approved a bank account's change may release a payment to it within its cooling period (TF-036), which the payment check names (SUP-164).
rationale: The approvers must fit the risk and the unit; and the person who changed a bank account is the last person who should pay into it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configuration that sends critical changes of high-tier suppliers to finance, When such a change is submitted, Then finance's approvers receive it.|Given a change to unit A's payment terms, When submitted, Then unit A's approvers receive it.|Given a change requested by a person who is also a configured approver, When they approve it, Then it is refused naming the segregation rule. (error case)|Given the approver of a bank change two days ago, When the payment check is asked for a release by them, Then the answer refuses them as the releaser, naming the rule. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rules 2 and 3). Map step CM-04.

title: Bank account changes
requirement: A bank account added or changed, from any source, is a critical change: it is approved, then verified, by the automated check (SUP-162) and by the call-back where it is required (SUP-163), and only then applied; it starts the cooling period (SUP-164). Only the supplier's primary contact may propose one from the supplier's side. When it applies, the supplier's primary contact and the buyer owner are told, and the change is announced to the contacts known before the change, through channels the change did not touch: their email addresses and phone numbers from before it, never ones given in it.
rationale: Bank account change fraud is the main payables risk; the announcement through old channels lets the real supplier say no before money moves.
acceptance_criteria: Given a primary contact adding a bank account in the portal, When submitted, Then a change request exists, and the account applies only after approval and verification.|Given a verification that fails, When it returns, Then the account does not apply and the request records why. (error case)|Given a bank change applied, When it applies, Then the contacts known before the change are told at the addresses they had before it, and the new account is in its cooling period.|Given a bank change sent with a new email address for the primary contact, When the announcement goes out, Then it goes to the address from before the change.|Given a contact who is not the primary contact, When they propose a bank change in the portal, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New in this area 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G5 and the pack's section 8.2, rule 8): with SUP-162 to SUP-164 it replaces SUP-023, retired, and keeps its notification of the primary contact and the buyer owner. Map steps CM-05 and CM-07.

title: Effective dates
requirement: A change may apply now or on a future date (a move to a new address next month); until then the record keeps its current value and the approved request waits. The record keeps its current values only; its field-level history shows each value with the dates it was valid (TF-062). Documents copy what they need when issued (an order keeps the address it was issued with), and a payment uses the bank account valid and verified on the payment date.
rationale: Suppliers announce moves and new accounts ahead; the change should be decided when it is known and apply when it is true.
acceptance_criteria: Given an address change approved for 1 December, When an order is issued on 20 November, Then it carries the old address; one issued on 2 December carries the new one.|Given a bank account change effective 1 December, When a payment is released on 25 November, Then it uses the old account.|Given a supplier's address changed twice this year, When its history is opened, Then each value shows with the dates it was valid.|Given a controlled or critical change with an effective date in the past, When submitted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 4, and section 8.5, decisions 2 and 3). Map step CM-06. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a controlled or critical change cannot be dated back, so a payment or an order is never made under a value that was not approved at the time.

title: Concurrency and one pending change per field
requirement: When a change applies, each field's old value must still be the current value; if another change came first, the field stops for review instead of overwriting. A field has at most one pending change: a second change to it waits until the first ends, and its requester is told why.
rationale: Two people correcting the same phone number from different sources must not overwrite each other in silence.
acceptance_criteria: Given two requests that read the same phone number and the first applies, When the second comes to apply, Then it stops for review with both values shown. (error case)|Given a pending change to the remit-to address, When a second change to it is submitted, Then it waits behind the first and the requester is told why.|Given the first request rejected, When decided, Then the waiting second moves to review.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rules 5 and 6). Map step CM-06.

title: Impact preview
requirement: Before a controlled or critical change is approved, its reviewers shall see the open documents that use the values it changes, as every product answers through the business layer's use of master records (BF-207), and decide whether open orders take the new values; the change's event carries that decision, and Orders applies it (ORD-011). Payments always use the bank account valid and verified on the payment date.
rationale: A reviewer who sees that forty open orders ship to the old address decides differently from one who does not.
acceptance_criteria: Given an address used by three open orders, When a reviewer opens the change, Then the three orders are listed.|Given a reviewer who chooses that open orders take the new address, When the change applies, Then its event names the address and that choice.|Given a product that does not answer the use of master records, When the preview is built, Then it names the product whose answer is missing, and the change can be approved only with a reason. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 7). Map step CM-03. Supplier management is the first product and never calls a later one (ADR-0042): the open documents come through BF-207, and the open orders take the new values through the event Orders hears. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a missing answer does not block a change but needs the reviewer's reason.

title: Notifications of changes
requirement: The supplier's primary contact and the buyer owner shall be told about every applied critical change, with the old and new values masked where they are sensitive; a bank change is also announced to the contacts known before it (SUP-205); the requester is told each field's outcome (SUP-203); and an uncontrolled change tells the buyer owner.
rationale: The people who would notice a wrong change must hear of it, and quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a legal name change applied, When it applies, Then the primary contact and the buyer owner are told, with the old and new names.|Given a notification to the primary contact that cannot be delivered, When it fails, Then the buyer owner is told and the failure is shown on the change request. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 8). Map step CM-07. Its notification keys are SUP-121's.

title: Signatures and history of changes
requirement: For tenants with Part 11 controls on, the approval of a critical change is an electronic signature (TF-063, TF-219), meaning approved or rejected, with re-authentication for a bank change; every applied change is in the supplier's field-level history (TF-062) with its source, its request and its deciders, sensitive values masked.
rationale: A bank or legal name change is the decision an auditor asks about first.
acceptance_criteria: Given Part 11 controls on, When a critical change is approved, Then the approval is a signature with the signer's name, the time and the meaning, linked to the request's version.|Given a bank change approved without re-authentication, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an applied change, When the supplier's history is opened, Then the field, the old and new values, the source and the request are shown, a bank account number masked.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 9). Map steps CM-04 and CM-07. Re-authentication for a bank change was decided on 2026-10-20 for SUP-023 (section 9) and stays.

title: Change measures
requirement: The product shall report pending change requests by age and source, rejection rates per field class, cycle times per class, and the changes made outside the tenant's business hours (TF-099), each flagged for review on its request.
rationale: A queue of old requests, a source rejected more than others, or a bank change at two in the morning each say something is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Given twelve pending requests, When the report runs, Then they are listed by age band and source.|Given a bank change submitted at 02:00, outside business hours, When submitted, Then it is flagged for review on its request and in the report.|Given a user without the supplier report permission, When the report is asked for, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.2, rule 10). Map steps CM-01 to CM-07.

title: Supplier documents and compliance expiry
requirement: Document types (name, issuer type, mandatory for publishing, expiry rule, expiry action: warn, block new orders, unpublish) shall be configured; supplier documents carry issue and expiry dates and attachments; a daily job shall apply expiry actions and notify the supplier and buyer 30, 14 and 1 days before expiry.
rationale: Compliance at all times.
acceptance_criteria: Given a document expiring in 14 days, When the job runs, Then supplier and buyer are notified.|Given an expired document with action "block new orders", When an order is created, Then it is refused naming the document. (error case)|Given a renewed document uploaded, When saved, Then the block is lifted.
notes: Was FF-030. Since 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps) a document about to expire triggers an information request (SUP-223), and the documents of an approved response become supplier documents (SUP-228).

title: Supplier questionnaires
requirement: Buyers shall send questionnaires (kernel forms) to suppliers for qualification and periodic review; responses shall be scored by evaluators and stored on the supplier with dates; questionnaires may be required for publishing.
rationale: Structured qualification.
acceptance_criteria: Given a required questionnaire unanswered, When publishing, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a response scored, When viewed on the supplier, Then score and date are shown.|Given a questionnaire sent, When the supplier logs in, Then it appears in their portal with status. (edge)
notes: Was FF-031. AC1 is marked as the error case it is (ADR-0041). Kernel forms are the kernel's forms engine, TF-242, a capability to be added. Retired 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps): questionnaires became periodic supplier information collection, SIM, on the forms engine (the pack's section 8.3), and qualification a status per scope (gap G2). Replaced by SUP-181 and SUP-221 to SUP-231.

title: Supplier risk flags
requirement: Buyers shall record risk flags on suppliers (type, severity, source, date, note) that show on supplier selection and may block new orders when severity is critical.
rationale: Manual risk management before any external data source.
acceptance_criteria: Given a critical flag, When an order is created, Then it is refused with the flag shown. (error case)|Given a medium flag, When a supplier is selected, Then a warning is shown.|Given a flag cleared, When saved, Then the history keeps it with the clearing reason.
notes: Was FF-039.

title: Supplier contact data protection
requirement: Supplier contacts and the supplier's portal users known to the tenant are personal data. Supplier management shall declare their fields in the kernel's data map (TF-196) with their purpose (managing the supplier relationship; receiving orders and payment advice) and their retention: the contact entry is kept until the relationship ends, then for the period the tenant sets, 2 years by default, and then anonymised; the records under a legal retention of their own (signed approvals, the audit trail, invoices, call-back records, the documents the contact sent) keep the person's name for as long as they are kept, with access restricted to those who may read them. The lawful basis is the contract with the supplier, recorded in the data map (TF-197). An access request returns what the tenant holds about a contact across its supplier records. An erasure request anonymises the contact entry, and leaves the records under a legal retention as they are. A contact who receives orders or payment advice cannot be erased while that role is theirs. A verification or screening provider that receives contacts' names is a sub-processor the tenant sees (TF-198).
rationale: Under the DPDP Act 2023 and the GDPR a supplier's contacts have the same rights as anyone; the audit trail of a bank change must still show who confirmed it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier contact, When the data map is opened, Then its fields show their purpose, retention and lawful basis.|Given an access request for a person who is a contact of two suppliers, When it is answered, Then both suppliers' data about the person are in the export.|Given an erasure request for a former contact, When executed, Then the contact entry's name, email and phone are anonymised, and the signed approvals and call-back records they took part in keep their name, for as long as those records are kept.|Given an erasure request for the contact who receives payment advice, When executed, Then it is refused until another contact takes that role. (error case)|Given a relationship that ended more than 2 years ago, When the retention job runs, Then its contact entries are anonymised, and an invoice and the audit trail that name a contact keep the name until their own retention ends.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G10). Map steps SM-04 and V7. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: only the contact entry is anonymised, 2 years after the relationship ends by default; records under a legal retention (signed approvals, the audit trail, invoices) keep the person's name for as long as they are kept (TF-066); the lawful basis is the contract, not consent. Its privacy requests run on the kernel's (TF-196, S6).

title: Information request templates
requirement: An information request template is a form template of the forms engine (TF-242) with its purpose (licence, certification, financial statements, insurance, tax declaration, sustainability, diversity, policy acknowledgement, qualification questionnaire); its sections, each with its reviewers; its questions, each mapped where useful to a field Supplier management declares mappable (TF-245: the supplier record, a supplier document type, a certification, a qualification scope, a custom field); attachments with issue and expiry dates; scores and weights; its outcome rules (SUP-229); and its non-response rule (SUP-224). Templates are versioned, and a request keeps the version it was sent with.
rationale: One template, built once, collects the same information from every supplier in the same shape, and knows which answers update which fields.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template with a question mapped to the expiry date of the supplier's insurance certificate, When saved, Then the mapping is listed with the field it updates.|Given a question mapped to a field Supplier management does not declare mappable, When saved, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)|Given a template changed after requests were sent, When an open request is opened, Then it shows the version it was sent with.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3). Map step SI-01. With SUP-222 to SUP-231 and SUP-181 it replaces SUP-042, retired.

title: Information requests and campaigns
requirement: A buyer, compliance or quality user shall send a template to one supplier, or run a campaign to a target set: by category, country, segment (PUR-026), risk tier (SUP-007), qualification scope (SUP-181), unit or visibility tags. The target is resolved when the campaign starts, and each supplier gets its own request; a supplier on hold or inactive gets none and is listed as left out with the reason.
rationale: A yearly certificate collection from three hundred suppliers is one campaign, not three hundred emails.
acceptance_criteria: Given a campaign to tier high suppliers in India, When it starts, Then each matching active supplier gets one request and the campaign lists them.|Given a supplier on hold in the target, When the campaign starts, Then it gets no request and is listed as left out, with the reason.|Given a target that resolves to no supplier, When the campaign is started, Then it is refused naming the target. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, point 1). Map steps SI-01 and SI-03.

title: Schedules and triggers
requirement: A request or campaign runs once, recurs (yearly, quarterly or another interval), or is triggered by an event: a supplier document about to expire (SUP-041), its lead time 45 days by default; a requalification falling due (SUP-181, SUP-183); a category added to the supplier; or a change of its risk tier (SUP-007). A trigger does not send a second request while one of the same template is open for the supplier.
rationale: The next collection is planned by the information's own life: a certificate's expiry, a qualification's term, a supplier's new risk.
acceptance_criteria: Given a yearly campaign started on 1 April, When the next 1 April comes, Then it runs again with its target resolved afresh.|Given an insurance certificate expiring in 45 days and a template triggered by its expiry, When the daily job runs, Then a request is sent to the supplier naming the expiring document.|Given an open request of the same template for the supplier, When a trigger fires again, Then no second request is sent. (error case)|Given a supplier whose risk tier rises to high, When it changes, Then the requests that tier requires are sent.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, point 2). Map steps SI-02 and SI-09. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: an expiry triggers a request 45 days before the expiry date by default.

title: Due dates, reminders, escalation and non-response
requirement: Each request shall have a due date. Reminders go to the supplier's contacts 7 days before it, on the day, and every 7 days after; a request overdue by the template's escalation days (14 by default) is escalated to the buyer owner; then the template's non-response rule applies: warn, block new orders, unpublish, or put the supplier on hold, as SUP-041's expiry actions do. The rule lifts when a response is approved.
rationale: A request without consequences is answered last; the consequence a supplier faces should be the one the information is worth.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request due on 30 June, When 23 June comes, Then the supplier's contacts are reminded.|Given a request overdue by 14 days, When the job runs, Then the buyer owner is told.|Given a template whose non-response rule blocks new orders, When its request is overdue past the escalation, Then an order for the supplier is refused naming the request. (error case)|Given the response approved, When decided, Then the block lifts.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, point 3). Map steps SI-03 and SI-09, and the reminders between SI-03 and SI-04. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: the reminder days and the escalation after 14 days are defaults, set per template.

title: Responding to an information request
requirement: The supplier shall answer in the portal (SPX-029) or through a one-time verified link sent to a known contact (TF-246, SPX-008). Drafts are saved; the form shows what is still missing; mapped answers come pre-filled with the current values and are confirmed or changed; attachments carry their issue and expiry dates. On submission the response is validated and scored.
rationale: Suppliers answer more and faster when the form already knows what the customer knows, saves their work, and works without a portal account for those who answer once a year.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mapped question pre-filled with the current bank name, When the supplier confirms it unchanged, Then no change is proposed for it.|Given a draft saved, When the contact returns, Then it resumes with what is still missing listed.|Given a required attachment missing, When submitted, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)|Given a response submitted, When it is scored, Then its score is the template's weighted sum and is kept with the response.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, point 4). Map steps SI-04 and SI-05. With TF-246 it works before the Supplier Network exists (S8); the portal's view of it is SPX-029, and with SPX-008 and SPX-029 it replaces SUP-102, retired.

title: Review per section
requirement: Each section shall be reviewed by its reviewers (finance for financial documents, quality for certificates), who approve, reject or return it, with comments per question for a return. A returned section goes back to the supplier and the rest waits. By default sections are decided independently: an approved section's answers count once the review ends, a rejected section's do not, and the request stays open for a new answer to the rejected section until it is answered or cancelled. A template may be marked all or nothing: then a rejected section rejects the whole response, with the reasons, and the request stays open for a new response. A response is approved when every section is approved.
rationale: Each team decides what it knows; a supplier fixes only what was returned.
acceptance_criteria: Given a response with a financial and a quality section, When finance approves the first, Then the second still waits for quality.|Given a section returned with a comment on one question, When the supplier opens the response, Then only that section can be edited and the comment shows beside the question.|Given every section approved, When the last approval is recorded, Then the response is approved and its application starts (SUP-227).|Given a person outside a section's reviewers, When they approve it, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a template decided section by section, a financial section approved and a quality section rejected, When the review ends, Then the financial answers are applied, the quality answers are not, and the supplier is asked again for the quality section only.|Given a template marked all or nothing and one section rejected, When the review ends, Then no answer of the response is applied and the request stays open for a new response. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, review point 2). Map step SI-06. Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: sections are decided independently by default; a template may be marked all or nothing, and then a rejected section rejects the whole response (AC5, AC6).

title: Applying approved answers through change management
requirement: When a response's review ends, the changed mapped answers of its approved sections (SUP-226) shall be applied automatically, by a change request from the source approved information response (SUP-201): uncontrolled and controlled fields apply at once, since the section's review approved them; critical fields still go through verification before they apply (a bank account from a form is verified like any other, SUP-205). The response links to its change request, and the change request to its response.
rationale: A reviewer should not retype what a supplier wrote and a reviewer approved; and no form, however reviewed, may put an unverified bank account on a supplier.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved response that changes the website and an address, When it is approved, Then one change request from the source approved information response applies both at once.|Given an approved response with a new bank account, When it is approved, Then the account is verified and applies only when the verification passes.|Given a mapped field that changed after the request was sent, When the change request comes to apply, Then that field stops for review instead of overwriting (SUP-207). (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, review point 3). Map step SI-08 and source C3 of the change management map. Change management is the only way a change reaches an approved supplier, and SIM applies through it.

title: Documents from responses
requirement: The attachments of a response's approved sections shall become supplier documents (SUP-041) of their document type, with their issue and expiry dates, so the next expiry triggers the next collection (SUP-223).
rationale: A certificate collected once must not be lost in a response; its expiry plans the next request.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved response with an ISO 9001 certificate valid to 31 March 2027, When approved, Then the supplier holds the document with that expiry, and its next request is planned 45 days before it.|Given a document that replaces an expired one, When applied, Then the expired document's block lifts (SUP-041).|Given an attachment whose expiry date is before its issue date, When submitted, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, review point 4). Map step SI-08.

title: Outcomes of a response
requirement: By its template's outcome rules, a response whose review ended shall set its outcomes from its approved sections: the qualification status of a scope (SUP-181), the evidence of a regulated qualification for the quality unit's signature (SUP-183), risk flags (SUP-043), and the supplier's scores. Each outcome names the response it came from.
rationale: A qualification questionnaire's purpose is the decision it supports; the system should take that decision as the template says, and show where it came from.
acceptance_criteria: Given a qualification questionnaire scored 82 with a pass mark of 70, When approved, Then the scope's qualification becomes qualified, naming the response.|Given a score below the pass mark, When approved, Then the qualification becomes disqualified or conditional by the template's rule, and the buyer owner is told.|Given an outcome rule for a regulated qualification, When the response is approved, Then the combination waits for the quality unit's signature and is not approved by the rule alone. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, review point 5). Map step SI-07.

title: The response record and its versions
requirement: The answers that map to no field shall be kept as the response record, versioned: each response to a recurring request is a version, and the supplier's 360 view (SUP-061) shows every response with its versions and the differences from the one before.
rationale: Sustainability or financial answers matter as a trend; this year's answer means more beside last year's.
acceptance_criteria: Given this year's and last year's sustainability responses, When compared, Then the changed answers are shown with both values.|Given an approved response, When anyone edits it, Then it is refused; a correction is a new version. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, review point 6). Map step SI-08.

title: Tracking requests and campaigns
requirement: A campaign shall show, per supplier and in total, its requests sent, opened, in progress, submitted, in review, returned, approved and overdue; a buyer may remind a supplier, extend a due date with a reason, or cancel a request with a reason. A supplier's 360 view (SUP-061) lists its open and past requests with their states.
rationale: A campaign is managed by its numbers: who has not opened it, who is stuck in review, who is overdue.
acceptance_criteria: Given a campaign to 50 suppliers with 20 approved and 5 overdue, When opened, Then the totals and each supplier's state are shown.|Given a due date extended without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a supplier's 360 view, When opened, Then its open and past requests are listed with their states.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the pack's section 8.3, tracking). Map steps SI-03 to SI-09.

title: Supplier 360 view and lists
requirement: Buyers shall see a supplier page with tabs (profile, addresses, contacts, sites, banks, documents, information requests and their responses with versions, qualifications, change requests, verification and screening results, performance, orders, receipts, invoices, contracts, catalogue, approvals, history), its risk tier and segment, and lists with filters by status, category, country, risk tier, segment and document expiry.
rationale: One place for the relationship.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier, When opened, Then all tabs load with counts.|Given a filter by documents expiring within 30 days, When applied, Then only matching suppliers appear.|Given a user without read permission, When opened, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a filter by risk tier high and segment strategic, When applied, Then only suppliers with both appear.
notes: Was FF-034. Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps): the tabs of the new areas take the place of questionnaires, and the lists filter by risk tier and segment (AC4).

title: Supplier performance indicators
requirement: The system shall compute per supplier and period: on-time acknowledgement rate, on-time delivery rate (receipt date versus need-by), receipt rejection rate, invoice accuracy (invoices held or rejected), and show them on the supplier and in reports.
rationale: Supplier management needs facts.
acceptance_criteria: Given orders and receipts in a quarter, When indicators compute, Then the rates match the underlying documents.|Given no activity, When viewed, Then indicators show "no data" not zero. (edge)|Given an indicator below a threshold, When evaluated, Then the supplier is flagged for review.|Given a user without the supplier performance permission, When indicators are requested, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-032. Orders, Receiving and Invoicing are later products, so the rates come from the events they publish (ADR-0042). Decision F-09 confirmed.

title: Supplier reports
requirement: Supplier master reports (status, categories, risk tiers, documents expiring, pending change requests, bank verifications, screening cases, qualifications falling due, information requests overdue) and performance indicators per period, with the onboarding measures (SUP-064) and the change measures (SUP-211).
rationale: Supplier management.
acceptance_criteria: Given documents expiring within 30 days, When the report runs, Then suppliers and documents are listed.|Given performance indicators, When run for a quarter, Then rates per supplier are shown.|Given export, When run, Then a file is produced. (edge)|Given a user without the supplier report permission, When run, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given qualifications falling due within 60 days, When the report runs, Then each supplier, scope and due date is listed.
notes: Was FF-163. Extended 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G11): the reports of the new areas and the measures of SUP-064 and SUP-211 (AC5).

title: Onboarding measures
requirement: Every step of every map of the process reference pack (SM-01 to SM-11, CM-01 to CM-07, SI-01 to SI-09) shall be timestamped when it starts and when it ends, and every wait marked as the supplier's or the tenant's. From them the product computes, per period, category, risk tier and unit: supplier setup time (an approved record to active, APQC measure 106476); onboarding cycle time from a complete request to transaction-ready, as median and 90th percentile, split into supplier waiting and internal waiting; first-pass completeness; self-service share; verified bank before first payment; duplicate rate; valid mandatory documents; requalification on time; and, for Indian suppliers, MSE classification coverage. Each is shown beside the pack's target (its section 5), whether it is met in words and not by colour alone.
rationale: What is not measured is not improved: onboarding is judged by its cycle time and its first-pass rate, and the split between supplier and internal waiting shows whom to chase.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request complete on day 0 and the supplier transaction-ready on day 9, with 5 days waiting for the supplier, When the measures compute, Then its cycle time is 9 days, 5 supplier waiting and 4 internal.|Given 10 suppliers onboarded in a quarter, 7 without a request for more information, When the measures compute, Then first-pass completeness is 70 percent.|Given a measure with a target, When shown, Then its value, its target and whether it is met are shown in words.|Given a step that started and has not ended, When the measures compute, Then it is listed as open and left out of the cycle times. (edge)|Given a user without the supplier report permission, When the measures are asked for, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G11); the pack's targets (its section 5) were accepted as proposed. Verified bank before first payment counts the payments Invoicing publishes (INV-043, ADR-0042); the strategic supplier share is the purchasing master's (PUR-026). Decided 2026-10-21 at the review: a wait is the supplier's while the supplier holds the next action (an invitation, a returned question, an information request), and the tenant's otherwise.

title: Notification keys of Supplier management
